title: The People Bring More Than Enough
text:
In the Book of Exodus, after the Israelites camped at Mount Sinai, Moses told them that a sanctuary was to be built, a portable tent of meeting called the tabernacle. He did not order a tax. He asked everyone whose heart moved them to bring an offering.

The people came. Men and women brought gold earrings and rings and brooches, silver and bronze, blue and purple and scarlet yarn, fine linen, goat hair, ram skins, acacia wood, oil, spices and precious stones. Women who were skilled spun yarn with their own hands. Others spun goat hair. The leaders brought onyx and gems for the priest's garments.

Moses appointed Bezalel and Oholiab, master craftsmen, to lead the work, along with every skilled person who was willing. Each morning the people kept bringing more gifts.

After a while the craftsmen left their tasks and came to Moses. The people are bringing much more than enough, they said, more than the work requires. So Moses had a message carried through the camp: no man or woman should make anything more as an offering. And the people were restrained from bringing any more, because what they had brought was already more than enough to finish the work.
lesson: People give generously to a shared project when they are invited rather than ordered. Pair willing contributors with skilled leaders and know when to say you have enough.
